paper.title: Rubric-Guided Self-Distillation: Post-Training Without Rubric Verifiers
paper.abstract: Rubrics have emerged as an alternative to RLVR in open-ended domains where a single ground-truth final answer is not available. Existing rubric-based training methods rely on an LLM verifier that scores each rollout against rubrics. This introduces substantial training-time overhead, exposes optimization to verifier-specific biases, and reduces rubric feedback to a sparse end-of-trajectory signal. We propose Rubric-Guided Self-Distillation (RGSD), a verifier-free training method in which the bas

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的是开放式任务里的一个具体瓶颈：当任务没有唯一标准答案时，后训练通常要把每个 prompt 配一套 rubric，再用外部 LLM judge 给整段回答打分，然后用 RL 去优化。问题不在于 rubric 本身，而在于“rubric + verifier + trajectory-level scalar reward”这条训练链路代价高、反馈稀疏、而且容易把 judge 的偏好和盲点一并学进去。论文想解决的是：能不能不再依赖训练时的 rubric verifier，只利用 rubric 本身，把模型在‘看见 rubric 时会答得更好’这一现象转成可训练信号，让学生模型学会在不显式看到 rubric 的情况下内化这些要求。
summary.importance: 对预训练/后训练接口的启发主要有三点。第一，它把原本偏 RL 的 rubric optimization 改写成了条件化自蒸馏，说明一部分所谓“需要 verifier 的开放式优化”其实可以退化成更稳定的 token-level learning。第二，它把奖励学习里的 credit assignment 问题，换成了逐 token 的分布匹配，这对长回答尤其重要，因为 rubric 满足与否往往由局部决策累积而成。第三，它提示一个更一般的方向：如果某种额外上下文能显著提升 base model 的条件分布，那么这类提升未必一定要通过 judge 或 preference model 才能传给部署时的模型，也可以通过 self-distillation 内化。贡献量级上，它不是替代所有 RL 的统一方案，但在 rubric-based open-ended post-training 这个子问题上，给出了一个更便宜、实现更简单、训练信号更密的基线，而且结果并不弱。
summary.technical_approach:
方法很直接，但设计上有几个关键点。RGSD 用同一个 base checkpoint 复制出 teacher 和 student。student 只看原始 prompt，按当前策略 on-policy 采样回答；teacher 冻结参数，但在输入里额外看到该 prompt 对应的 rubric，并在 student 已生成前缀的条件下，对下一个 token 给出分布。训练目标不是让 student 拟合 teacher 的整句参考答案，而是对 student 自己采样出来的轨迹做逐 token 分布蒸馏。

这样做有几个含义。其一，它保留了 on-policy 性质：teacher 不是在自己偏好的轨迹上教学，而是在 student 实际会走到的状态上给局部纠偏信号，这比离线蒸馏更贴近 policy improvement。其二，teacher 和 student 来自同一底模，唯一差别是 teacher 看到了 rubric，因此蒸馏的不是“更强模型的知识”，而是“额外条件信息带来的分布改写”。其三，论文没有直接用 KL，而是用了 clipped Jensen-Shannon divergence。这里的考虑是 teacher 和 student 初期可能分歧很大，纯 KL 容易被尖锐分布主导，训练不稳；JS 更对称，clipping 进一步限制极端 token 上的梯度，减少蒸馏时的爆炸更新。

从全文描述看，teacher 的 rubric 输入不是机械地把 checklist 原样拼进去，而是包成与 prompt 同一轮 user message，并加一段过渡指令，要求回答满足这些要求但不要显式提 rubric。这一点很重要，因为目标不是让模型学会复述 rubric，而是把 rubric 约束转成自然回答风格。论文还做了 enrichment source 的对比：把 teacher 额外条件换成 reference response，效果不如直接给 rubric，说明结构化评价标准比单个示例更适合作为蒸馏条件。

和 judge-based GRPO 的区别也很清楚。GRPO 需要每个 prompt 采样多条 rollout，用 judge 打分，再做组内相对优势估计；RGSD 只需要单条 rollout，没有外部 judge，也没有 trajectory-level reward。代价是它依赖一个前提：base model 在“显式看到 rubric”时确实能显著提升。如果这个 conditioning lift 很弱，RGSD 的上限也会受限。
summary.experiments:
实验覆盖 4 个底模：Qwen-2.5-Instruct 3B、7B，以及 Qwen3-Thinking 4B、8B；任务域是 medical 和 science，并同时看 in-distribution 与 out-of-distribution 评测。论文先给出一个很关键的前置观察：同一个 base model，只要把 per-prompt rubric 放进上下文，回答质量相对未条件化版本可提升 30–45 个百分点。这基本构成了 RGSD 可行性的经验基础。

主结果上，RGSD 与 judge-based GRPO 整体接近，且略有优势：medical 域平均提升为 +6.1 分，对比 GRPO 的 +5.9；science 域为 +4.9，对比 +4.5。这里的提升是相对各自 base model 的 rubric-based 评测增益。论文强调，RGSD 达到这些结果时不需要任何训练时 judge call，而且每个 prompt 只生成一条响应，不像 GRPO 需要多条 rollout 再评分，因此训练吞吐和工程复杂度都更好。

一个有意思的现象出现在 Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct：RGSD 在大约只有 GRPO 一半的响应长度时就达到峰值质量。这说明 token-level distillation 不只是省 judge 成本，也可能抑制 RL 常见的 length inflation。对开放式生成来说，这个点很实际，因为很多 rubric-based RL 会通过更长、更面面俱到的回答去“刷分”。

消融里最重要的两组。第一组是 judge strength：当 GRPO 使用更强、更贵的 judge 时，在部分设置下可以超过 RGSD。这说明 RGSD 不是无条件优于 verifier-based RL，它更像是在“中等 judge 质量 + 高训练成本”区间里提供了更好的性价比。第二组是 enrichment signal：teacher 额外看到 rubric，比看到 reference response 更有效，说明 rubric 提供的是更可泛化、更可组合的约束信息，而不是单一答案模板。

从论文给出的结论看，RGSD 的收益在不同模型家族上都存在，但强度并不完全一致。Thinking 模型和 Instruct 模型的行为差异值得留意：如果底模本身已经较擅长根据长上下文约束调整生成，RGSD 更容易工作；如果底模对 rubric 条件不敏感，蒸馏信号会变弱。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议是先抓三处。第一，看引言里的 Table 1 和相关描述，确认“rubric conditioning lift”到底有多大；这是整篇方法成立的前提。第二，看方法图和 Algorithm 1，重点理解 teacher 不是生成参考答案，而是在 student rollout 上做逐 token 分布监督。第三，看 judge strength ablation 和 enrichment ablation，这两部分决定了这篇工作的边界：它在哪些条件下能替代 GRPO，在哪些条件下还不行。

如果只花 20–30 分钟，建议顺序是：Introduction → Figure 1 / Method 主体 → 主结果表 → 两个 ablation。阅读时重点想两个问题：为什么 on-policy distillation 比离线 SFT 更合适；为什么 rubric 作为条件比 reference answer 更强。若要深挖，可以继续看附录里的 teacher/judge prompt 模板，因为这类方法对输入包装很敏感，很多效果差异可能来自 prompt 设计而不只是目标函数。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets a specific weakness of rubric-based post-training for open-ended tasks. When there is no single verifiable final answer, current practice is to attach a prompt-specific rubric, sample responses, ask an external LLM judge to score rubric satisfaction, and optimize with RL. The bottleneck is not the rubric itself, but the training loop built around it: expensive verifier calls, sparse trajectory-level rewards, and optimization pressure toward the judge’s own biases. The paper asks whether the rubric can be internalized without a training-time verifier, by exploiting a simple empirical fact: the same base model often performs much better when the rubric is placed in context.
summary_en.importance: The main value is conceptual. It reframes part of open-ended RL-style optimization as conditional self-distillation rather than reward maximization. That matters for post-train design because it replaces sparse scalar rewards with dense token-level supervision, which is a cleaner fit for long-form generation where rubric satisfaction emerges from many local decisions. It also suggests a broader recipe: if extra conditioning information reliably shifts the model toward better behavior, that shift may be distilled into the deployment policy without keeping a verifier in the loop. This is not a universal replacement for RL, but within rubric-based post-training it is a strong efficiency-oriented alternative with a simpler training stack and competitive quality.
summary_en.technical_approach:
RGSD instantiates two copies of the same base checkpoint: a frozen teacher and a trainable student. The student sees only the prompt and samples an on-policy rollout. The teacher sees the prompt, the rubric, and the student prefix at each decoding step, and produces a next-token distribution used as the supervision target. Training is done by matching the student to the rubric-conditioned teacher token by token on the student’s own trajectory.

Several design choices matter. First, this is on-policy distillation rather than offline imitation. The teacher does not supervise its own preferred trajectory; it provides local corrective distributions on states the student actually visits. That makes the update closer to policy improvement than standard response distillation. Second, teacher and student share the same underlying model family and initialization. The gain does not come from a stronger teacher model, but from exposing the teacher to extra task structure through the rubric. Third, the paper uses a clipped Jensen-Shannon divergence instead of a plain KL loss. The motivation is stability: early in training, teacher and student can disagree sharply, and a one-sided KL can overemphasize low-entropy teacher peaks. A symmetric JS objective with clipping reduces extreme gradients and makes the distillation signal less brittle.

The paper also pays attention to how the rubric is injected. The rubric is wrapped into the same user turn as the prompt, followed by a short transition telling the teacher to satisfy the criteria without explicitly mentioning them. This is important because the target behavior is not rubric recitation, but natural responses that implicitly satisfy the checklist. An additional ablation compares rubric conditioning against conditioning on a reference response; the rubric is stronger, which suggests that structured criteria are a better source of transferable supervision than a single exemplar.

Compared with judge-based GRPO, the difference is sharp. GRPO needs multiple rollouts per prompt, judge scoring, and group-relative advantage estimation. RGSD uses a single rollout, no external judge, and no trajectory-level reward. The trade-off is that RGSD depends on a meaningful conditioning lift from the base model. If the model barely improves when shown the rubric, the distillation ceiling will be limited.
summary_en.experiments:
The experiments cover four base models: Qwen-2.5-Instruct 3B and 7B, plus Qwen3-Thinking 4B and 8B. The domains are medical and science, with both in-distribution and out-of-distribution evaluation. A key preliminary result is that simply showing the rubric to the base model improves rubric-based scores by roughly 30 to 45 percentage points over the unconditioned base. That observation is the empirical foundation of the method.

On the main comparison, RGSD is competitive with, and slightly ahead of, judge-based GRPO on average. In medical tasks, the average gain is +6.1 points versus +5.9 for GRPO. In science, it is +4.9 versus +4.5. The paper emphasizes that RGSD reaches these numbers without any training-time judge calls and with only one generated response per prompt, whereas GRPO requires multiple rollouts plus grading. So the quality is similar, but the training loop is materially cheaper and simpler.

One notable behavioral result appears on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct: RGSD reaches peak quality at about half the response length of GRPO. This is more than a cost detail. It suggests that token-level distillation may reduce the length inflation often seen in RL-style optimization, where models learn to satisfy rubrics by becoming verbose.

The most informative ablations are twofold. First, judge strength matters. When GRPO uses a stronger and more expensive judge, it can outperform RGSD in some settings. That sets the boundary of the method: RGSD is not strictly better than verifier-based RL, but it is attractive when verifier quality is moderate and verifier cost is high. Second, the enrichment source matters. Conditioning the teacher on the rubric works better than conditioning on a reference response, indicating that explicit criteria provide more compositional and generalizable guidance than a single target answer.

The gains are present across model families, but not uniformly. The paper hints that models already good at using long-context constraints are better candidates for RGSD, because the whole method relies on the teacher being meaningfully improved by rubric exposure.
summary_en.reading_guide:
For a quick read, focus on three parts. First, inspect the early table and discussion showing the rubric-conditioning lift. Without that result, the whole method is much less compelling. Second, read the method figure and algorithm carefully to understand that the teacher is not generating a gold response; it is providing token-level distributions on the student’s own rollout. Third, read the two main ablations: judge strength and enrichment source. Those sections define where RGSD can replace GRPO and where it cannot.

A practical 20–30 minute path is: Introduction, the main method section with Figure 1 and Algorithm 1, the headline result tables, then the ablations. While reading, keep two questions in mind: why on-policy distillation should work better than offline SFT here, and why a rubric is a stronger conditioning signal than a reference answer. If there is time for a deeper pass, check the appendix prompts for teacher and judge formatting. Methods like this are often sensitive to prompt packaging, and some of the observed gains may depend on that interface design as much as on the loss itself.

recommendation.zh: 只看方法图和 GRPO 对比即可；思路干净，但领域偏窄，关键是确认 teacher 是否只是泄漏 rubric 偏好。
recommendation.en: Skim the method figure and GRPO comparison; the idea is clean, but the key question is whether the teacher merely leaks rubric preferences.

从论文给出的结论看，RGSD 的收益在不同模型家族上都存在，但强度并不完全一致。Thinking 模型和 Instruct 模型的行为差异值得留意：如果底模本身已经较擅长根据长上下文约束调整生成，RGSD 更容易工作；如果底模对 rubric 条件不敏感，蒸馏信号会变弱。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议是先抓三处。第一，看引言里的 Table 1 和相关描述，确认“rubric conditioning lift”到底有多大；这是整篇方法成立的前提。第二，看方法图和 Algorithm 1，重点理解 teacher 不是生成参考答案，而是在 student rollout 上做逐 token 分布监督。第三，看 judge strength ablation 和 enrichment ablation，这两部分决定了这篇工作的边界：它在哪些条件下能替代 GRPO，在哪些条件下还不行。

如果只花 20–30 分钟，建议顺序是：Introduction → Figure 1 / Method 主体 → 主结果表 → 两个 ablation。阅读时重点想两个问题：为什么 on-policy distillation 比离线 SFT 更合适；为什么 rubric 作为条件比 reference answer 更强。若要深挖，可以继续看附录里的 teacher/judge prompt 模板，因为这类方法对输入包装很敏感，很多效果差异可能来自 prompt 设计而不只是目标函数。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets a specific weakness of rubric-based post-training for open-ended tasks. When there is no single verifiable final answer, current practice is to attach a prompt-specific rubric, sample responses, ask an external LLM judge to score rubric satisfaction, and optimize with RL. The bottleneck is not the rubric itself, but the training loop built around it: expensive verifier calls, sparse trajectory-level rewards, and optimization pressure toward the judge’s own biases. The paper asks whether the rubric can be internalized without a training-time verifier, by exploiting a simple empirical fact: the same base model often performs much better when the rubric is placed in context.
summary_en.importance: The main value is conceptual. It reframes part of open-ended RL-style optimization as conditional self-distillation rather than reward maximization. That matters for post-train design because it replaces sparse scalar rewards with dense token-level supervision, which is a cleaner fit for long-form generation where rubric satisfaction emerges from many local decisions. It also suggests a broader recipe: if extra conditioning information reliably shifts the model toward better behavior, that shift may be distilled into the deployment policy without keeping a verifier in the loop. This is not a universal replacement for RL, but within rubric-based post-training it is a strong efficiency-oriented alternative with a simpler training stack and competitive quality.
summary_en.technical_approach:
RGSD instantiates two copies of the same base checkpoint: a frozen teacher and a trainable student. The student sees only the prompt and samples an on-policy rollout. The teacher sees the prompt, the rubric, and the student prefix at each decoding step, and produces a next-token distribution used as the supervision target. Training is done by matching the student to the rubric-conditioned teacher token by token on the student’s own trajectory.

Several design choices matter. First, this is on-policy distillation rather than offline imitation. The teacher does not supervise its own preferred trajectory; it provides local corrective distributions on states the student actually visits. That makes the update closer to policy improvement than standard response distillation. Second, teacher and student share the same underlying model family and initialization. The gain does not come from a stronger teacher model, but from exposing the teacher to extra task structure through the rubric. Third, the paper uses a clipped Jensen-Shannon divergence instead of a plain KL loss. The motivation is stability: early in training, teacher and student can disagree sharply, and a one-sided KL can overemphasize low-entropy teacher peaks. A symmetric JS objective with clipping reduces extreme gradients and makes the distillation signal less brittle.

The paper also pays attention to how the rubric is injected. The rubric is wrapped into the same user turn as the prompt, followed by a short transition telling the teacher to satisfy the criteria without explicitly mentioning them. This is important because the target behavior is not rubric recitation, but natural responses that implicitly satisfy the checklist. An additional ablation compares rubric conditioning against conditioning on a reference response; the rubric is stronger, which suggests that structured criteria are a better source of transferable supervision than a single exemplar.

Compared with judge-based GRPO, the difference is sharp. GRPO needs multiple rollouts per prompt, judge scoring, and group-relative advantage estimation. RGSD uses a single rollout, no external judge, and no trajectory-level reward. The trade-off is that RGSD depends on a meaningful conditioning lift from the base model. If the model barely improves when shown the rubric, the distillation ceiling will be limited.
summary_en.experiments:
The experiments cover four base models: Qwen-2.5-Instruct 3B and 7B, plus Qwen3-Thinking 4B and 8B. The domains are medical and science, with both in-distribution and out-of-distribution evaluation. A key preliminary result is that simply showing the rubric to the base model improves rubric-based scores by roughly 30 to 45 percentage points over the unconditioned base. That observation is the empirical foundation of the method.

On the main comparison, RGSD is competitive with, and slightly ahead of, judge-based GRPO on average. In medical tasks, the average gain is +6.1 points versus +5.9 for GRPO. In science, it is +4.9 versus +4.5. The paper emphasizes that RGSD reaches these numbers without any training-time judge calls and with only one generated response per prompt, whereas GRPO requires multiple rollouts plus grading. So the quality is similar, but the training loop is materially cheaper and simpler.

One notable behavioral result appears on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct: RGSD reaches peak quality at about half the response length of GRPO. This is more than a cost detail. It suggests that token-level distillation may reduce the length inflation often seen in RL-style optimization, where models learn to satisfy rubrics by becoming verbose.

The most informative ablations are twofold. First, judge strength matters. When GRPO uses a stronger and more expensive judge, it can outperform RGSD in some settings. That sets the boundary of the method: RGSD is not strictly better than verifier-based RL, but it is attractive when verifier quality is moderate and verifier cost is high. Second, the enrichment source matters. Conditioning the teacher on the rubric works better than conditioning on a reference response, indicating that explicit criteria provide more compositional and generalizable guidance than a single target answer.

The gains are present across model families, but not uniformly. The paper hints that models already good at using long-context constraints are better candidates for RGSD, because the whole method relies on the teacher being meaningfully improved by rubric exposure.
summary_en.reading_guide:
For a quick read, focus on three parts. First, inspect the early table and discussion showing the rubric-conditioning lift. Without that result, the whole method is much less compelling. Second, read the method figure and algorithm carefully to understand that the teacher is not generating a gold response; it is providing token-level distributions on the student’s own rollout. Third, read the two main ablations: judge strength and enrichment source. Those sections define where RGSD can replace GRPO and where it cannot.

A practical 20–30 minute path is: Introduction, the main method section with Figure 1 and Algorithm 1, the headline result tables, then the ablations. While reading, keep two questions in mind: why on-policy distillation should work better than offline SFT here, and why a rubric is a stronger conditioning signal than a reference answer. If there is time for a deeper pass, check the appendix prompts for teacher and judge formatting. Methods like this are often sensitive to prompt packaging, and some of the observed gains may depend on that interface design as much as on the loss itself.

recommendation.zh: 只看方法图和 GRPO 对比即可；思路干净，但领域偏窄，关键是确认 teacher 是否只是泄漏 rubric 偏好。
recommendation.en: Skim the method figure and GRPO comparison; the idea is clean, but the key question is whether the teacher merely leaks rubric preferences.

paper.title: World Model Self-Distillation: Training World Models to Solve General Tasks
paper.abstract: Pretrained video generators are promising visual world models that exhibit emergent task-solving abilities; however, their reliance on detailed textual descriptions limits their direct use for planning and decision-making. Existing approaches either outsource this reasoning to language or vision-language models, or rely on supervised fine-tuning with paired task-execution videos, which are costly to collect and difficult to scale. We propose a scalable framework that elicits task-solving ability

summary.core_problem: 解决预训练视频生成世界模型依赖详细文本描述无法直接用于规划决策、监督微调数据成本高难以扩展的问题
summary.importance: 范式创新+方法创新，提出无需人工标注任务视频的可扩展框架，将视频扩散模型的生成能力转化为通用任务解决能力
summary.technical_approach: 提出自蒸馏结合强化学习的框架：1）用视觉-语言模型为无标注场景图像生成候选任务与分步解决方案；2）用解决方案条件预训练视频扩散模型（Demonstrator）生成执行视频；3）将Demonstrator的行为蒸馏到仅依赖图像和短任务提示的Executor模型，实现指令条件的任务求解
summary.experiments: 摘要截断未给出具体模型参数量、训练数据规模与基线对比数值，核心贡献为可扩展的训练框架设计

summary_en.core_problem: Addresses two limitations of pretrained video generator world models: reliance on detailed textual descriptions which blocks direct use for planning, and high cost of supervised fine-tuning data that is hard to scale
summary_en.importance: Paradigm + methodological innovation: proposes a scalable annotation-free framework to transfer generation capability of video diffusion models into general task-solving ability
summary_en.technical_approach: A self-distillation + reinforcement learning framework: 1) A VLM generates candidate tasks and step-by-step solutions for unlabeled scene images; 2) The solutions condition a pretrained video diffusion model (Demonstrator) to produce execution videos; 3) Distill Demonstrator's behavior into an Executor that only takes image and short task prompt for instruction-conditioned task solving
summary_en.experiments: Abstract truncated, no specific parameter scale, training data size or baseline comparison numbers provided; core contribution is the scalable training framework design

recommendation.zh: 视频世界模型的弱监督蒸馏思路可参考，仅看方法部分的框架设计即可，无直接可复用的LLM预训练结论
recommendation.en: Weakly-supervised distillation idea for video world models is worth referencing, only read the framework design in method section, no directly reusable conclusions for LLM pretraining

paper.title: RLCSD: Reinforcement Learning with Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation
paper.abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) provides dense, token-level supervision for reasoning models by aligning a model's own distribution with the distribution it produces under privileged context, typically a verified solution. However, we show that the learning signal drawn from this distributional gap concentrates on style tokens rather than task-bearing ones, as the hinted model tends to produce more direct, shorter outputs. We term this pathology \emph{privilege-induced style drift}, which des

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作解决 RLVR 和 on-policy self-distillation 中的 token 级信用分配问题：只用最终 reward 太稀疏，而用带正确答案提示的自蒸馏信号又容易学到风格变化，而不是学到真正和正确性相关的 token。
summary.importance: 这是一篇 post-training 方法论文，但对预训练研究也有参考意义。它把“更密的 token 级训练信号”与“verifier 给出的结果级方向”结合起来，试图减少长推理训练中的不稳定、长度塌缩和无效风格模仿。对基座训练的启发在于：当监督信号来自同一模型在不同条件下的 log-prob 差异时，条件信息会带来非任务因素，需要设计对照项把这些因素消掉。
summary.technical_approach: 已有 OPSD 方法把同一模型分成 student 和 privileged teacher：student 只看问题和已生成前缀，teacher 额外看到正确参考解。训练信号是 teacher 与 student 在当前 token 上的 log-prob 差值。作者指出，这个差值不只包含正确性信息，还包含 privilege-induced style drift，例如更短、更确定、更少探索性措辞，以及格式和连接词概率的变化。RLCSD 的做法是同时给 teacher 一个正确提示和一个错误提示，计算两种条件下相对 student 的 log-prob 差值，再相减得到 contrastive token signal。正确和错误提示使用相同模板，因此共享的风格偏移会被抵消，剩下的信号更偏向任务相关 token。训练时，这个 token 级信号不是替代 GRPO 的 query-level advantage，而是作为调制项作用在 outcome reward 给出的 advantage 上，并通过额外设计避免反转 advantage 的方向或在序列聚合中被稀释。
summary.experiments: 实验覆盖 Qwen3 的 1.7B、4B、8B 三个规模，以及 Olmo-3-7B-Think。任务包括数学推理 AMC23、AIME24、AIME25，以及 Knights & Knaves 逻辑推理的分布内和分布外难度。RLCSD 相比 GRPO，以及 OPSD、SDPO、SRPO、RLSD 等 on-policy self-distillation baseline，在测试 benchmark 上表现更稳定。作者强调两类现象：一是 RLCSD 能维持较稳定的 entropy 和 response length；二是其他 OPSD 方法容易出现训练不稳定、entropy 和长度异常增长，或者过早缩短回答长度，从而限制后期推理能力。消融实验显示，contrastive 设计可以插入已有 OPSD 方法并带来改进。给定内容中没有提供逐 benchmark 的具体分数表，因此不宜过度解读提升幅度。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读，约 25 到 35 分钟。重点看 Section 3 的目标函数和调制方式，尤其是 contrastive signal 如何定义、如何接入 GRPO advantage，以及为什么不直接把 token signal 当作独立监督。再看 Figure 1 中 token 排名、长度和 entropy 曲线，它们解释了 style drift 的训练后果。实验部分可重点看 ablation：正确/错误提示是否必须同模板、contrastive 信号能否迁移到其他 OPSD 变体、长度控制是否来自方法本身而不是奖励偏置。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses token-level credit assignment in RLVR and on-policy self-distillation. Outcome rewards in GRPO are sparse for long reasoning traces, while privileged self-distillation can produce dense token signals that are contaminated by style changes induced by the privileged context.
summary_en.importance: This is mainly a post-training method, but it is relevant to foundation-model training because it studies how to construct cleaner dense supervision from model-internal probability differences. The key lesson is that conditioning a model on extra information changes not only correctness-related probabilities but also style, length, and discourse behavior. A useful token-level signal needs a control condition, otherwise the model may optimize toward formatting and brevity rather than reasoning quality.
summary_en.technical_approach: Prior OPSD methods use the same model as both student and teacher. The student conditions on the query and generated prefix, while the teacher also sees a correct reference solution. The token signal is the teacher-student log-probability gap. RLCSD adds a contrastive control: the teacher is conditioned once on a correct hint and once on an incorrect hint, preferably sampled from the same rollout group. The method computes the two teacher-student gaps and subtracts them. Because the correct and incorrect hints share the same prompt template, style shifts common to both conditions are suppressed, leaving a signal more aligned with task-bearing tokens. This contrastive signal is then used to modulate the GRPO outcome-level advantage rather than replace it. The design keeps the verifier-provided direction intact and prevents the token signal from being washed out during sequence-level aggregation.
summary_en.experiments: The experiments cover Qwen3 at 1.7B, 4B, and 8B scales, plus Olmo-3-7B-Think. Tasks include mathematical reasoning on AMC23, AIME24, and AIME25, and logical reasoning on Knights & Knaves under both in-distribution and out-of-distribution difficulty. RLCSD is reported to outperform GRPO and several OPSD baselines, including OPSD, SDPO, SRPO, and RLSD. The main empirical finding is not only higher benchmark performance but also better training dynamics: RLCSD preserves response length and maintains more stable entropy, while competing OPSD variants may become unstable or shrink responses too early. The provided text does not include full per-benchmark score tables, so the safest reading is about the mechanism and training dynamics rather than exact margins.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in 25–35 minutes. Spend most time on the method section: the definition of the contrastive token signal, how it is combined with the GRPO advantage, and why it is not used as a standalone supervised loss. Figure 1 is useful because it connects token rankings, style drift, length, and entropy dynamics. In the experiments, focus on ablations: whether matched templates matter, whether the contrastive principle improves other OPSD variants, and whether the length stability comes from the method rather than reward shaping.

recommendation.zh: 这篇值得看，不是因为又多了个 RL 变体，而是它把 OPSD 的脏信号拆开了；先看 token 分析和长度分布，若成立，内部 RL recipe 应立刻补这个对照。
recommendation.en: Worth reading not because it adds yet another RL variant, but because it decomposes the dirty signal inside OPSD; start with the token analysis and length distributions, and if they hold up, add this control to your internal RL recipe.

paper.title: HERO: Hindsight-Enhanced Reflection from Environment Observations for Agentic Self-Distillation
paper.abstract: Reinforcement learning typically improves multi-turn agent capabilities through the terminal outcome of the trajectories, which makes it difficult to determine credit assignments for each intermediate turns. Recent on-policy self-distillation methods offer a promising alternative by converting privileged feedback into dense token-level supervision through a self-teacher. Our study is motivated by the unexpected performance degradation observed when naively extending this paradigm to multi-turn s

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作解决多轮 agent 自蒸馏中的 credit assignment 问题：终局反馈或成功轨迹很难对齐到每一步当前决策上下文，导致蒸馏信号失真甚至退化。
summary.importance: 贡献属于后训练方法改进。它不是新的 RL 范式，但指出了多轮环境中 privileged feedback 与局部决策错位这一常见问题，并给出更细粒度的 hindsight 监督构造方式。
summary.technical_approach: 作者提出 HERO。核心做法是在 rollout 完成后，利用“下一步环境观测”作为与当前动作局部对齐的反馈来源，对每个 observation 生成紧凑的 turn-level diagnosis，再把这些诊断转成学生模型可学习的密集监督信号。相比直接用成功轨迹或终局结果做 teacher，HERO 强调局部可执行、与决策时刻对齐的反思。
summary.experiments: 摘要未给出完整模型规模和数据规模。实验重点是多轮 agent 场景中的 self-distillation，对比 naive on-policy self-distillation。作者声称 naive 扩展会出现性能下降，而 HERO 能缓解这种退化，说明局部 hindsight 反馈比终局反馈更适合多轮 credit assignment。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses credit assignment in multi-turn agent self-distillation, where terminal outcomes or successful trajectories are poorly aligned with each intermediate decision context.
summary_en.importance: This is a post-training method improvement rather than a new RL paradigm. Its main value is identifying a common failure mode in multi-turn self-distillation and proposing a more locally aligned supervision signal.
summary_en.technical_approach: HERO performs hindsight-enhanced reflection after each rollout. It uses the next environment observation as locally aligned feedback for the preceding action, converts observations into compact turn-level diagnoses, and then distills these diagnoses into dense supervision for the student model. The key idea is to replace coarse terminal feedback with context-aligned hindsight feedback.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract does not provide full model or data scale details. The experiments focus on multi-turn agent settings and compare against naive on-policy self-distillation. The main reported finding is that naive extension degrades performance, while HERO mitigates this by improving local credit assignment.

recommendation.zh: 不是 pretrain 论文，但它点中了多轮蒸馏最常见的坑：反馈与决策时刻错位；只看方法图和误差分析，别对泛化结论下太重注。
recommendation.en: Not a pretraining paper, but it nails a real failure mode in multi-turn distillation: feedback-decision misalignment; read the method sketch and error analysis, not as a broad new prior.

paper.title: The Role of Feedback Alignment in Self-Distillation
paper.abstract: Conditioning a language model on additional context, such as feedback on a previous attempt, typically improves its response. Self-distillation trains the model to retain this improvement when the context is not present. The method works by matching the model's output distribution under two settings: a student that sees only the question, and a self-teacher that also sees the context. What the model learns therefore depends on what context the self-teacher receives, yet the design of this contex

summary.core_problem: 论文研究自蒸馏中的反馈形态如何影响学习信号。自蒸馏让同一个模型同时扮演 student 和 self-teacher：student 只看问题，self-teacher 看问题加额外上下文。训练目标是让 student 匹配 self-teacher 的输出分布。关键问题是：这个额外上下文应该是什么？论文把问题放在数学推理中，比较三种信号：GRPO 的二值最终奖励、参考解答、以及与模型自身推理轨迹逐步对齐的 critique。
summary.importance: 这篇论文的价值在于把“反馈质量”和“反馈对齐”区分开。参考解答通常是完整且正确的，但它不一定沿着模型自己的推理轨迹展开，因此在自蒸馏中会产生较分散的 token-level 分布移动。逐步对齐的反馈虽然不直接给出强 teacher logits，也不需要训练过程奖励模型，却能把更新集中到错误附近的 token。对 reasoning post-training 来说，这提供了一条介于 RLVR 和过程监督之间的路径：保留 on-policy、自教师、无需外部 logits 的优点，同时获得比 rollout-level reward 更细的 credit assignment。
summary.technical_approach: 方法建立在 self-distillation objective 上。模型先在问题 x 上生成自己的推理轨迹 y。student 分布是 πθ(·|x,y<t)，self-teacher 分布是 πθ(·|x,c,y<t)，其中 c 是额外反馈上下文。训练最小化两者在每个 token 位置的 divergence，并对 teacher 分支 stop-gradient。已有分析表明，当 divergence 取 KL 类形式时，梯度可以写成类似 policy gradient 的形式，但 advantage 不再是 GRPO 那种整条 rollout 共享的标量，而是每个 token 一个 A_t^SD，用来衡量上下文 c 对下一 token 分布的局部影响。论文的核心设计是 StepAlignFB：冻结 critic 读取 solver 的实际推理轨迹，生成逐步对齐的 critique，指出哪一步出了问题、为什么错、应该如何修正。它不同于 RefSol。RefSol 给出标准解，但标准解和 solver 轨迹在表述、分解顺序、局部选择上经常不一致，即使 solver 的某些步骤是对的，teacher context 也可能推动分布向另一条解法迁移。StepAlignFB 则贴着 solver 的轨迹给反馈，使 self-teacher 的分布变化更容易落在真正需要修正的位置。
summary.experiments: 实验在数学推理场景中采用 solver-critic 设置，critic 冻结。比较对象包括：二值最终奖励的 GRPO、以参考解答作为上下文的 self-distillation、以及 StepAlignFB。论文报告 StepAlignFB 在所有 aggregation-style accuracy 指标上优于 GRPO 和 RefSol。更有信息量的是 per-token advantage 分析：StepAlignFB 的分布移动集中在错误相邻 token 附近，表现出类似过程监督的定位能力；RefSol 的信号更分散，因为参考解答与模型轨迹不对齐；GRPO 的 advantage 对同一 rollout 内所有 token 恒定，难以判断是哪一步导致最终错误。当前材料中没有给出具体参数规模、训练 token 数、数据规模和各 benchmark 的精确数值，因此不宜补写未确认数字。
summary.reading_guide: 建议精读 Background 中 GRPO 与 self-distillation 梯度形式的推导，尤其是 rollout-level advantage 和 token-level self-distillation advantage 的对比。方法部分应重点看 StepAlignFB 的 prompt 结构、critic 输入输出格式、反馈如何与 solver trace 对齐。实验部分优先看 Section 4 的主结果表、aggregation accuracy 的定义、per-token advantage 可视化，以及 RefSol 失败案例。值得深挖的问题有三个：第一，StepAlignFB 的收益来自 critique 内容还是来自轨迹对齐；第二，critic 质量下降时信号是否仍然稳定；第三，不同 divergence 选择是否会改变 advantage 的稀疏度和更新强度。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper asks what kind of context should be used in self-distillation. In this setup, the same model is used twice: a student conditioned only on the question, and a self-teacher conditioned on the question plus extra context. The training objective matches the student distribution to the contextualized self-teacher distribution. The central question is whether the context should be a scalar reward, a reference solution, or feedback aligned to the model’s own reasoning trace.
summary_en.importance: The main contribution is the separation between feedback quality and feedback alignment. A reference solution can be correct and complete, but it may follow a different trajectory from the model’s own rollout, which makes the induced token-level signal diffuse. Step-aligned critique produces a more localized update around the parts of the trace where the reasoning goes wrong. For reasoning post-training, this is a useful middle ground between RLVR and process supervision: it keeps the on-policy and teacher-free properties of self-distillation, avoids access to external teacher logits, and still yields token-level credit assignment.
summary_en.technical_approach: The method builds on a standard self-distillation loss. The solver samples a reasoning trace y for a question x. The student distribution is πθ(·|x,y<t), while the self-teacher distribution is πθ(·|x,c,y<t), where c is additional context. The model minimizes a per-token divergence between these two distributions, with stop-gradient on the teacher branch. Prior analysis shows that, for KL-style divergences, the gradient resembles a policy-gradient update, but the advantage is token-specific rather than constant across the whole rollout as in GRPO. The proposed context, StepAlignFB, is generated by a frozen critic that reads the solver’s actual trace and produces step-by-step critique aligned to that trace. This differs from using a reference solution. A reference solution may be high quality, but it often diverges from the solver’s path in wording, decomposition, or intermediate choices. Step-aligned feedback instead addresses the rollout the model actually produced, so the contextual teacher shifts its distribution near the relevant errors.
summary_en.experiments: The experiments are conducted in mathematical reasoning with a solver-critic setup and a frozen critic. The paper compares three conditions: GRPO with a binary final reward, self-distillation using the reference solution as context, and self-distillation using step-aligned feedback. StepAlignFB is reported to outperform both GRPO and RefSol on all aggregation-style accuracy metrics. The more diagnostic result is the per-token advantage analysis: StepAlignFB concentrates distributional shifts around error-adjacent tokens, RefSol produces a broader and less localized signal, and GRPO assigns the same advantage to every token in a rollout. The supplied material does not include exact benchmark scores, model sizes, data scale, or token counts, so those numbers should not be inferred.
summary_en.reading_guide: Read the background derivation carefully, especially the comparison between GRPO’s rollout-level advantage and the token-level advantage induced by self-distillation. Then focus on the construction of StepAlignFB: the critic prompt, the alignment between critique and solver trace, and how the feedback is inserted into the self-teacher context. In the results section, prioritize the main accuracy table, the definition of aggregation-style metrics, and the per-token advantage visualizations. The most useful questions to track are whether the gains come from critique content or trace alignment, how robust the method is to critic errors, and whether the choice of divergence changes the sparsity and strength of the update.

recommendation.zh: 非常干净的 ablation，证明了在自蒸馏/RL 中，与模型自身轨迹对齐的 step-by-step critique 远胜于给标准答案或标量 reward，对合成推理数据极具实操价值。
recommendation.en: A very clean ablation showing that in self-distillation/RL, step-by-step critique aligned with the model's own trace vastly outperforms reference solutions or scalar rewards; highly actionable for synthesizing reasoning data.

paper.title: PBSD: Privileged Bayesian Self-Distillation for Long-Horizon Credit Assignment
paper.abstract: Long-horizon agentic tasks pose a fundamental credit assignment challenge for outcome-base reinforcement learning: trajectory-level rewards verify final correctness but provide limited guidance on which intermediate reasoning steps or tool interactions contribute to the outcome. The difficulty is especially pronounced in multi-turn search agents, where successful trajectories may contain misleading actions and failed trajectories may contain valuable evidence-gathering steps. We propose PBSD (Pr

summary.core_problem: 解决长时程 agent 任务中 outcome-only RL 难以做细粒度 credit assignment 的问题，尤其是成功轨迹里混有坏步骤、失败轨迹里混有好步骤时，最终奖励几乎不给有效训练信号。
summary.importance: 这属于后训练阶段的 RL 信号设计创新。对预训练研究员的价值在于，它提供了一种把稀疏终局验证信号转成 token/step 级训练信号的思路，可反哺对 reasoning trace 学习信号质量的理解。
summary.technical_approach: 作者提出 PBSD（Privileged Bayesian Self-Distillation）。核心做法是引入一个 answer-conditioned 的 privileged teacher，与普通 student 形成 likelihood ratio；再用 Bayes 规则把难以直接估计的 posterior-to-prior answer ratio，转写成可分解的 token 级证据分数。通过自回归分解，这个贝叶斯证据可以分配到中间推理步骤和工具调用上，从而在只有最终可验证答案的情况下做更细粒度的 credit assignment。
summary.experiments: 摘要未给出完整模型规模，但任务设定聚焦 multi-turn search / long-horizon agent。主要 baseline 应是 outcome-based RL 或 group-level reward 方法。论文声称 PBSD 能在稀疏最终奖励下更稳定地区分有价值与误导性的中间步骤。若看正文，重点应核查 teacher 是否引入额外信息泄漏、likelihood ratio 估计是否稳定，以及在不同 horizon 下是否优于简单 advantage shaping。
summary.authors_note: 作者名单包含 Lei Song、Jiang Bian、Bo Zhao，属于做 RL 与 agent 学习信号的团队；从题目和方法看，更偏强化学习与长时程 agent 后训练，而非预训练本体。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper tackles fine-grained credit assignment in long-horizon agent tasks, where outcome-only RL provides almost no useful signal because successful trajectories contain bad steps and failed ones may still contain useful evidence-gathering actions.
summary_en.importance: This is a post-training RL signal-design contribution. Its value to pretraining researchers is that it offers a way to convert sparse terminal verification into token- or step-level learning signals, which matters for reasoning-trace supervision quality.
summary_en.technical_approach: PBSD (Privileged Bayesian Self-Distillation) introduces an answer-conditioned privileged teacher and uses a likelihood-ratio view. By Bayes' rule, it rewrites the hard posterior-to-prior answer ratio into a tractable student-vs-teacher likelihood ratio. With autoregressive decomposition, the Bayesian evidence is assigned to intermediate reasoning steps and tool interactions, enabling finer credit assignment under only final verifiable rewards.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract does not expose full model scales, but the setting is multi-turn search and long-horizon agent tasks. The natural baselines are outcome-based RL and group-level reward methods. The main empirical claim is better discrimination between useful and misleading intermediate actions under sparse rewards. When reading, the key checks are whether the privileged teacher leaks information and whether the likelihood-ratio estimate remains stable across horizons.
summary_en.authors_note: The author list includes Lei Song, Jiang Bian, and Bo Zhao, suggesting a team with RL and agent-learning-signal background. The work is more about long-horizon agent post-training than pretraining proper.

recommendation.zh: 不是 pretrain，但 credit assignment 写得像样；先看贝叶斯重写那一节，若 teacher 泄漏控制干净，可借去做 reasoning trace 级训练信号。
recommendation.en: Not pretraining, but the credit-assignment formulation is worth a look; read the Bayesian rewrite first, and only trust it if the privileged-teacher leakage is tightly controlled.

paper.title: World Models Meet Language Models: On the Complementarity of Concrete and Abstract Reasoning
paper.abstract: World models and multimodal large language models (MLLMs) provide complementary capabilities for predicting future outcomes from static visual observations. World models can generate concrete visual rollouts of possible futures, while MLLMs can reason abstractly over questions, goals, and rules. However, generated rollouts are stochastic and may be visually plausible but task-incorrect, making it necessary to determine when visual simulation is useful, whether a rollout is credible, and how it s

summary.core_problem: 如何让多模态大语言模型 (MLLM) 学会判断何时调用世界模型进行视觉模拟，并验证和整合模拟结果以辅助抽象推理？
summary.importance: 探讨了世界模型（具体视觉模拟）与 MLLM（抽象推理）的互补性，提出了受控的具体推理范式，并构建了相关 Benchmark 和训练方法。
summary.technical_approach: 将问题形式化为受控的具体推理，模型需要学会调用、验证和整合视觉未来模拟。提出了特权未来同策略自蒸馏 (PF-OPSD) 方法，在训练期间利用真实的未来视频作为特权信息指导模型学习。
summary.experiments: 构建了两个人类验证的 Benchmark：VRQABench（可控空间前瞻）和 OpenWorldQA（开放域物理预测）。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自澳门大学等机构，关注多模态推理和世界模型。

summary_en.core_problem: How to enable Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to learn when to invoke world models for visual simulation, and how to verify and integrate the simulation results to aid abstract reasoning?
summary_en.importance: Explores the complementarity between world models (concrete visual simulation) and MLLMs (abstract reasoning), proposes a controlled concrete reasoning paradigm, and constructs related benchmarks and training methods.
summary_en.technical_approach: Formulates the problem as controlled concrete reasoning, where the model learns to invoke, verify, and integrate visual future simulations. Proposes Privileged-Future On-Policy Self-Distillation (PF-OPSD), which uses ground-truth future videos as privileged information during training to guide the model.
summary_en.experiments: Constructs two human-verified benchmarks: VRQABench for controllable spatial lookahead and OpenWorldQA for open-domain physical prediction.
summary_en.authors_note: Authors are from the University of Macau and other institutions, focusing on multimodal reasoning and world models.

recommendation.zh: 探讨了 MLLM 与 World Model 结合的范式，通过自蒸馏让模型学会何时调用和信任视觉模拟，对探索多模态 System 2 推理有启发，值得看其训练 recipe。
recommendation.en: Explores the paradigm of combining MLLMs with World Models, using self-distillation to teach models when to invoke and trust visual simulations; inspiring for exploring multimodal System 2 reasoning, worth checking the training recipe.

paper.title: When Should the Teacher Move? Temporal Coupling and Stability in Self On-Policy Distillation
paper.abstract: Self on-policy distillation trains a student policy against a teacher derived from its own parameter history, yet the teacher's update schedule -- which governs the \emph{temporal coupling} between teacher and student -- has not been systematically studied as a stability variable. Through a controlled schedule sweep on Qwen3-8B, we establish that \emph{isolation periods}, defined as complete teacher freezing between updates, are the key structural property enabling stable learning, not teacher a

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作研究的是自蒸馏式 on-policy post-training 里一个常被当作实现细节、但其实直接决定稳定性的变量：teacher 什么时候更新。设定里 teacher 不是外部强模型，而是 student 自己的历史快照，因此 teacher 与 student 的时间耦合会不断变化。问题不在于 teacher“老不老”，而在于它是否在一段时间内与 student 保持真正隔离。论文要解决的核心点有两个：第一，系统辨认哪些 teacher update schedule 会让自蒸馏从“纠偏锚点”退化成“自我确认”；第二，在长时训练下，如何避免固定刷新周期带来的单次错误 refresh 把坏策略永久写入 teacher，进而触发不可逆能力塌缩。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究者而言，这篇论文虽然落在 post-training，但价值不只是 RL recipe 调参。它把“目标网络/teacher 更新频率”从经验超参提升为训练动力学变量来分析，和预训练里 EMA target、BYOL/Mean Teacher、self-training、甚至 MoE router 稳定性问题有共通结构。最重要的结论是：稳定性主要来自 isolation period，而不是 teacher age。这个判断很有分量，因为很多工作习惯用 EMA 作为默认平滑器，认为只要 teacher 足够滞后就能稳定；这里给出的证据是，连续软跟踪即使平均滞后相同，长期仍会因污染累积而失去纠偏能力。另一个有启发的点是 state-oblivious collapse：固定周期在短程实验里看起来最优，拉长训练后却会因一次时机错误的 refresh 直接崩掉。这类“短程看不出、长程才暴露”的失稳模式，对任何依赖历史副本做自举的训练流程都值得警惕。
summary.technical_approach:
方法上分两部分。第一部分是诊断框架。训练目标由 GRPO 风格的 reward optimization 加上 teacher-student distillation 组成，蒸馏项用 top-k JSD 配合 importance-sampling correction 近似。围绕 teacher schedule，论文比较了两类典型机制：一是 hard refresh，每 M 步把 student 全量拷贝到 teacher，然后完全冻结；二是 EMA，每步按系数 α 软更新。作者还专门构造了 lag-aligned EMA baseline，用来控制 teacher age，使比较不被“平均滞后不同”混淆。诊断指标包括 temporal KL structure、refresh shock、length-tail risk。前者看 teacher 与 student 分布关系如何随时间演化；refresh shock 看 refresh 前后训练信号是否出现突变；length-tail risk 则把长回答尾部风险当作早期失稳信号，捕捉 reward 看不出的退化。

第二部分是提出 CGTR，Consolidation-Gated Teacher Refresh。它保留 hard refresh 的结构性优点，即 refresh 之间 teacher 完全冻结，确保 isolation period 存在；但不再按固定时钟刷新，而是要求满足联合门控条件才允许 teacher 移动。文中给出的门控核心包括 reward improvement condition 和 length-tail safety condition。前者要求 student 的进步不是噪声波动，而是已经形成可复制的收益提升；后者避免在长度分布异常、尾部风险升高时把不稳定行为写入 teacher。这样做的关键不是“更聪明地估计 teacher 年龄”，而是把 refresh 从 clock-driven 变成 state-dependent。相比 EMA，它避免持续污染；相比固定 hard refresh，它避免在错误时刻做不可逆拷贝。
summary.experiments:
实验主体基于 Qwen3-8B，作者先做了 100-step schedule sweep，核心发现是：只要存在完整 isolation period，训练显著更稳；而仅仅让 teacher 变老但持续软跟踪，并不能复现这种稳定性。也就是说，lag-aligned EMA 即便在平均滞后上对齐 hard refresh，结果仍不如后者。长时训练实验进一步显示固定短周期 hard refresh 会出现 state-oblivious collapse：在短 horizon 上表现最好的 schedule，训练拉长后会因一次不合时宜的 refresh 出现灾难性能力损失，而且之后难以恢复。

任务上覆盖 Chemistry、Biology、Physics、ToolUse 四个环境。论文给出的结论是，CGTR 用同一组超参在四个任务上都拿到最好分数，并且实现 zero collapse。这里最值得看的是它不是单任务调出来的 schedule，而是统一参数集跨任务稳定。消融方面，作者区分了“teacher age”和“isolation”两个因素，证明真正起作用的是后者；同时也分析了只加 reward gate 或只看长度风险时的不足，说明联合门控比单一条件更稳。摘要里没有完整数字表，但从正文描述看，重点不在小幅平均分提升，而在把长程训练中的崩溃率降到 0，并维持四任务一致收益。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议是先抓三件事。第一，看 Introduction 和 schedule analysis，明确作者要反驳的不是“teacher 越老越好”，而是“没有隔离就没有锚点”。第二，看 100-step schedule sweep 和 lag-aligned EMA 对比图，这部分决定论文是否成立。第三，看长时训练曲线，尤其是 fixed hard refresh 在后期突然崩掉的案例，这比平均分更有信息量。

如果时间有限，优先看 Figure 1 以及分析 temporal KL / refresh shock / length-tail risk 的章节，预计 20–30 分钟能抓住主线。值得深挖的点有两个：一是 top-k JSD 蒸馏近似在 on-policy 场景下是否会放大 refresh shock；二是 CGTR 的门控信号是否可以推广到更一般的 target network 更新，比如 self-training、RLAIF 中的 reference policy、甚至 continual pretrain 中的 teacher replay 机制。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies a stability variable in self on-policy distillation that is usually treated as an implementation detail: when the teacher should move. Here the teacher is not an external stronger model but a historical copy of the student itself, so the teacher-student relation is governed by temporal coupling. The central question is not how old the teacher is, but whether it remains structurally independent long enough to act as a corrective anchor. The paper addresses two linked issues: which teacher update schedules preserve stable learning, and how to avoid long-horizon failures where a badly timed refresh writes transiently corrupted behavior into the teacher and then reinforces that corruption through subsequent distillation.
summary_en.importance: Although this is a post-training paper, its value extends beyond RL recipe tuning. It turns teacher update scheduling into a training-dynamics object, which is relevant to target networks, EMA teachers, self-training, and any setup that bootstraps from historical model states. The main result is sharp: stability comes from isolation periods, not teacher age. That matters because EMA is often used as a default stabilizer under the assumption that sufficient lag is enough. The evidence here argues otherwise: continuous soft tracking still accumulates contamination over long horizons and eventually loses corrective power. The second important contribution is the identification of state-oblivious collapse: a fixed refresh interval can look optimal in short runs yet fail catastrophically in longer training because one refresh happens at the wrong moment. That lesson is broadly useful for long-horizon optimization pipelines.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The paper has two technical layers. First, it builds a diagnostic framework for teacher scheduling. The training objective combines a GRPO-style reward term with a teacher-student distillation term, where the KL regularizer is approximated by a top-k Jensen-Shannon divergence with importance-sampling correction. The study compares two canonical update rules: hard refresh, which copies the student into the teacher every M steps and freezes the teacher in between; and EMA, which updates the teacher continuously with coefficient alpha. To isolate the role of temporal structure from simple lag, the authors also construct a lag-aligned EMA baseline.

The diagnostics are centered on temporal KL structure, refresh shock, and length-tail risk. Temporal KL tracks how teacher and student distributions evolve relative to each other. Refresh shock measures the discontinuity introduced when the teacher is updated. Length-tail risk is used as an early warning signal for instability that may not be visible in reward alone.

Second, the paper proposes Consolidation-Gated Teacher Refresh, or CGTR. CGTR keeps the main structural advantage of hard refresh: the teacher is fully frozen between updates, so genuine isolation periods exist. But refreshes are no longer triggered by a fixed clock. Instead, a refresh is allowed only when joint conditions are satisfied, notably a reward-improvement condition and a length-tail safety condition. The first aims to ensure that the student has actually consolidated progress rather than exhibiting noisy fluctuations. The second prevents unstable long-tail behavior from being copied into the teacher. This makes teacher movement state-dependent rather than time-dependent. Compared with EMA, it avoids chronic contamination; compared with fixed hard refresh, it avoids irreversible bad copies at the wrong time.
summary_en.experiments:
The main experiments are run on Qwen3-8B. A 100-step schedule sweep shows the key result: schedules with complete isolation periods are consistently more stable, while simply increasing teacher lag without isolation does not recover the same behavior. In particular, lag-aligned EMA still underperforms hard refresh despite matched average lag, which supports the claim that isolation rather than age is the causal factor.

Long-horizon experiments reveal the paper’s main failure mode, state-oblivious collapse. A fixed hard-refresh schedule that looks strong in short training can fail later because one refresh captures the student during a transient bad state, after which the corrupted teacher keeps reinforcing the damage. The paper evaluates four tasks: Chemistry, Biology, Physics, and ToolUse. CGTR, with a single hyperparameter setting, achieves the best score on all four and reports zero collapse. The most informative ablations separate teacher age from isolation and show that the latter is the decisive ingredient. Additional analyses indicate that using only reward gating or only length-based safety is weaker than the joint gating rule. The emphasis is less on small average gains and more on eliminating catastrophic long-run failures.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Start with the introduction and the schedule analysis section. The key claim is not that older teachers are better, but that teachers need periods of full independence to remain useful. Then read the 100-step schedule sweep and the lag-aligned EMA comparison carefully; that is the empirical core of the paper. After that, focus on the long-horizon plots showing sudden collapse under fixed hard refresh. Those curves carry more information than aggregate scores.

If reading time is limited, prioritize Figure 1 and the sections on temporal KL, refresh shock, and length-tail risk. Around 20 to 30 minutes should be enough to extract the main argument. Two deeper follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind: whether the top-k JSD approximation interacts with refresh shock in nontrivial ways, and whether CGTR-style state-dependent updates can generalize to other target-network settings such as self-training, reference-policy updates in RLHF/RLAIF, or continual pretraining with teacher replay.

recommendation.zh: 对自蒸馏（如 RLHF/DPO 中的 reference model 更新）的稳定性给出了很好的机制解释，特别是揭示了 'isolation periods' 的重要性，对做 alignment 的同学很有启发。
recommendation.en: Provides a good mechanistic explanation for the stability of self-distillation (e.g., reference model updates in RLHF/DPO), especially revealing the importance of 'isolation periods', highly inspiring for alignment researchers.

institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

paper.title: Physics-Guided Policy Optimization with Self-Distillation
paper.abstract: Self-distilled policy optimization (SDPO) has become a popular paradigm for LLM post-training, where a model learns from its own predictions conditioned on privileged information. SDPO, however, is sensitive to how much each update step should be trusted: corrections from a self-teacher can be highly informative on some batches and misleading on others, and applying them uniformly with a fixed step size can destabilize training. Drawing inspiration from viscous-fluid dynamics and formalizing the

summary.core_problem: 在 SDPO（self-distilled policy optimization）/OPD 这类“自当老师”的后训练里，teacher 信号的可靠性随训练阶段与采样前缀分布漂移而剧烈变化；如果仍用固定学习率/固定信号权重做密集 token 级纠错，容易把“有用纠错”和“噪声纠错”一视同仁，导致梯度被极端 token 奖励或错误纠错主导，出现不稳定甚至训练崩溃。论文要解决的是：如何在 SDPO 更新中为每一步/每个 batch 自适应地调节更新幅度，使训练在后期仍稳定，同时不牺牲早期的快速收益。
summary.importance: 对基座预训练本身的直接贡献有限（更偏 post-train / policy optimization 稳定性），但它触及一个与持续训练/continual pretrain 共通的核心问题：当监督信号的“可信度”随时间变化时，固定步长会把优化推入不稳定区。PGPO 给出一个可实现的“信息量驱动步长调制”范式：用 teacher-student 一致性（互信息估计）作为局部可靠性指标，把它显式注入到优化动力学里。对做 RLVR/OPD/SDPO 的团队更有现实价值；对预训练研究的启发主要在于：可以把数据质量/标签可靠性/teacher 置信度统一成一个可微的步长或权重控制信号，而不是只做样本过滤。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是给每次参数更新乘一个信息调制系数 ρ_k，而不是固定学习率。论文先把 SGD/Adam 的离散更新写成 SDE 的 Euler–Maruyama 近似（弱收敛意义），用“粒子在粘性介质中运动”的类比引出非牛顿粘度：局部粘度由当前 batch 的信息量决定。

具体实现：在一次 SDPO 迭代里，student 先生成响应并得到反馈；self-teacher 在“带特权信息”的条件下给出纠错分布/信号。然后估计 student 预测与 teacher（在反馈条件下）的互信息 I_k（文中把它作为“这次纠错到底提供了多少新增信息”的代理）。最后用指数映射做步长乘子：ρ_k = min(exp(α·I_k), ρ_max)，把原本的梯度更新变成 θ_{k+1} = θ_k − η · ρ_k · g_k（对 Adam 也是等价地缩放有效步长）。

与已有稳定化手段的区别：
- 不做 hard routing（按对错分流）或 hard filtering（按置信度丢样本），而是连续地缩放更新幅度；因此在“部分有用、部分有害”的 batch 上更平滑。
- 不依赖额外 reward anchor 或外部 critic，而是用 teacher-student 的信息一致性做内生信号。
- 形式上更像“自适应全局 step-size controller”，而不是 token-level reweighting；优点是实现简单、对优化器侵入小，缺点是粒度较粗，无法直接定位到哪些 token 在制造噪声。
summary.experiments:
全文给出的实验更像 preliminary：主要展示 PGPO 在 SDPO 训练中能减少不稳定现象（如 loss spike、collapse）并保持收益。当前提供的正文片段没有给出可复述的关键数字（模型规模、数据规模、具体指标提升幅度、与哪些 baselines 的对比表格）。从叙述看，作者强调两点证据链：
1) 训练动态：互信息低的 batch 会被自动降步长，从而抑制“错误纠错/极端 token 奖励”导致的梯度爆炸；
2) 理论侧：给出 order-1 weak SDE 近似，说明这种缩放可以被解释为改变扩散/漂移项的有效强度。

如果需要判断方法是否可用，最关键的是看：互信息估计的方差、计算成本、以及在不同任务/不同 SDPO 变体（含 RLVR）下是否稳定复现。就目前文本信息，证据强度偏中等。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议（约 20–30 分钟）：
- 先看 Introduction 里对 SDPO 不稳定来源的拆解：prefix drift、uniform correction、extreme token-level rewards，这部分决定它到底在解决什么。
- 重点看 Preliminaries 到算法框（PGPO pseudocode）：I_k 如何定义/估计、ρ_k 的形式、以及对 Adam 这类自适应优化器如何落地。
- 如果时间够，再看 SDE 推导相关段落与附录：它是否真的给出了可检验的预测，还是仅作为类比。

精读不建议投入太多，除非你正在做 OPD/SDPO/RLVR 的稳定训练；那时需要逐行核对互信息估计细节与额外开销，并复现其训练曲线对比。

summary_en.core_problem: SDPO/OPD-style post-training uses a self-teacher with privileged feedback to provide dense token-level corrections. As training progresses, the student’s rollout distribution drifts away from the teacher’s conditioning distribution, making some corrections highly informative and others actively misleading. Applying a uniform update magnitude (fixed LR / fixed correction weight) turns this into a credit-assignment and stability problem, often manifested as loss spikes or collapse. The paper targets a practical question: how to adapt the update size online so that SDPO remains stable in later stages without giving up early-stage gains.
summary_en.importance: This is primarily a post-training stability paper rather than a pretraining recipe contribution. Still, it highlights a general optimization theme relevant to continual pretraining: when supervision reliability is non-stationary, fixed step sizes are brittle. PGPO proposes an “information-controlled step-size” mechanism, using a teacher–student mutual-information proxy as a reliability signal. The main value for pretraining researchers is conceptual: instead of hard filtering low-quality signals, treat signal quality as a continuous controller that modulates optimization dynamics.
summary_en.technical_approach:
PGPO multiplies each optimization step by an information-dependent scalar. The paper frames SGD as an Euler–Maruyama discretization of an SDE (weak approximation) and borrows a viscous-fluid analogy: local viscosity (hence effective step size) should vary with how informative the current teacher signal is.

Algorithmically, for each SDPO iteration: (1) the student generates responses and receives feedback; (2) the self-teacher, conditioned on privileged feedback, produces correction targets; (3) compute an information signal I_k, described as a mutual-information estimate between the student predictions and the feedback-conditioned teacher; (4) convert it into a step-size multiplier ρ_k = min(exp(α·I_k), ρ_max); (5) scale the gradient update (or the effective step in Adam) by ρ_k.

Key distinction from common stabilizers: it avoids hard routing/filtering and instead applies smooth, batch-level attenuation/amplification; it does not require an external critic/reward anchor, relying on internal teacher–student agreement as the control signal. The trade-off is granularity: batch-level scaling is simple but cannot localize which tokens are noisy.
summary_en.experiments: The experiments are presented as preliminary evidence that PGPO reduces SDPO instability (e.g., suppressing spikes/collapse) while preserving learning progress. In the provided full-text excerpt, there are no reproducible headline numbers (model size, data scale, exact metric deltas, full baseline tables). The empirical story is mainly training-dynamics driven: low mutual-information batches get down-weighted, preventing extreme token-level signals from dominating updates. For adoption, the critical missing details to verify are: how MI is estimated in practice, its variance/cost, and whether results hold across tasks and SDPO+RLVR variants.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim plan (20–30 minutes):
- Read the Introduction carefully for the failure-mode taxonomy (prefix drift, uniform correction on already-correct samples, extreme token-level rewards).
- Focus on the PGPO algorithm box and the definition/estimation of I_k; this determines whether the method is implementable.
- If relevant, check the SDE derivation/appendix to see whether it yields actionable predictions or is mainly motivational.

Deep reading is only warranted if you actively train OPD/SDPO/RLVR systems and need a lightweight stability controller; then you should audit MI estimation, overhead, and sensitivity to α and ρ_max.

recommendation.zh: 用互信息动态调节自蒸馏步长的思路挺有意思，SDE 的推导可以看看，但实验规模较小，作为 post-train 稳定性的一个 trick 备查。
recommendation.en: The idea of dynamically adjusting self-distillation step size using mutual information is interesting; the SDE derivation is worth a look, but the experiments are small-scale, keep it as a trick for post-train stability.

paper.title: Self-Distilled Policy Gradient
paper.abstract: On-policy self-distillation, where a language model conditions on privileged context to supervise its own generations, is a promising source of dense supervision for sparse-reward reinforcement learning. Actually, it can be instantiated as an auxiliary full-vocabulary student-to-teacher reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence loss. We therefore propose SDPG, a self-distilled policy-gradient framework that combines group-relative verifier advantages with normalized standard deviation, exact full-voca

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的是 RLVR 里一个很具体但长期存在的矛盾：verifiable reward 只在序列末端给出稀疏的对错信号，而推理模型的学习需要更细粒度的 token 级训练信号。已有 on-policy self-distillation 试图用“带特权上下文的同模型 teacher”给 student 提供稠密监督，但它通常被当成一个额外蒸馏 loss 来看，缺少清晰的策略梯度解释，也容易在 teacher 信号不可靠时把模型往局部合理、全局错误的轨迹上推。SDPG 的核心问题就是：如何把 full-vocabulary self-distillation 以严格的 policy-gradient 形式并入 KL-regularized RLVR，使稀疏 verifier reward 和稠密 privileged teacher signal 能同时工作，而且训练更稳。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究本身，它不是直接改 pretrain recipe，而是更像 pretrain↔post-train 接口上的一篇方法论文：它把“自蒸馏提供稠密 token 监督”这件事从经验技巧推进到可分析的 RL 目标，并明确指出 teacher signal 的收益与风险边界。价值主要有三点。第一，它给 full-vocab reverse KL self-distillation 一个局部精确的策略梯度解释，这有助于理解为什么这类方法能补足 sparse reward。第二，它强调 privileged context 不是无条件有益，若没有 verifier 约束，teacher 可能放大全局错误轨迹上的局部高概率 token，这对 reasoning post-training 很关键。第三，它提出的 gating 和 coefficient schedule，本质上是在做训练信号质量控制，这一点对以后把合成监督、过程监督、latent hint 等信号并入 RL 或 mid-training 都有参考意义。贡献量级更接近“把一类做法讲清楚并做稳”，不是范式替换。
summary.technical_approach:
方法上，SDPG 建立在 KL-regularized policy optimization 框架上，目标里有三类信号。第一类是标准 RLVR 的 outcome reward。它沿用 group-based rollout，并用 group-relative advantage；文中还强调用 normalized standard deviation 处理组内 reward 归一化，缓解 reward 方差和全 0/全 1 组带来的不稳定。第二类是 privileged on-policy self-distillation：同一个模型分成两个分支，student 用可部署上下文生成，teacher 看到额外特权信息，例如 demonstration、答案或 reasoning path。关键不是只加一个 KL，而是使用 exact full-vocabulary reverse KL，形式是 D_KL(p_t || SG[q_t])，其中 q_t 停梯度。作者证明，对固定 rollout prefix，这个 reverse KL 的 student-side gradient 与一个 detached-sampling policy-gradient update 局部等价，其 token advantage 可以写成 centered log teacher/student ratio，也就是以 log(q/p) 为核心、再减去对应分布级 KL 均值做中心化。这个推导的意义在于：蒸馏不再只是“模仿 teacher”，而是可以看成对每个 token 的 advantage shaping。第三类是 reference-policy KL regularization。作者采用基于 RPG 的 KL 正则化形式，主文聚焦未归一化 forward / reverse KL 到固定 reference policy，用来限制策略漂移，避免 privileged teacher 和 verifier 共同驱动下的更新过猛。

在稳定性设计上，SDPG 有两个明确的工程控制件。其一是 positive-advantage gating：只在 verifier advantage 为正时启用或强化 distillation 信号，避免 teacher 在负样本轨迹上继续灌输局部模式。其二是 warmup-decay schedule：蒸馏系数先升后降，前期帮助模型获得稠密学习信号，后期逐步让 verifier 主导，减少 teacher ceiling 对 student 探索空间的压制。和 RLSD 这类把 teacher 信号揉进 clipped ratio 的方法相比，SDPG 更强调把蒸馏项作为一个精确、全词表、可解释的辅助 policy-gradient 信号，而不是仅仅作为 PPO/GRPO surrogate 的修饰项。
summary.experiments:
从全文给出的实验设置看，作者主要比较了三类基线：纯 RLVR/GRPO 类方法、已有 self-distillation 类方法，以及带不同正则和稳定器的 SDPG 变体。结论层面比较清楚：SDPG 在性能和训练稳定性上都优于 RLVR 与自蒸馏基线，尤其是在早期训练阶段负 advantage 较多、reward 稀疏时更稳。论文强调的收益不是单点峰值，而是更平滑的 learning curve、更少的 collapse/震荡，以及更高的最终 verifier pass rate。

更值得看的是消融。第一，exact full-vocabulary reverse KL 明显优于只在 sampled token 上做近似蒸馏，说明 teacher 分布的“暗知识”在 reasoning token 选择上确实有用。第二，去掉 positive-advantage gating 后，训练会更容易受错误 teacher signal 干扰，尤其在全局错误轨迹上出现性能回退。第三，去掉 warmup-decay schedule，或者让蒸馏系数始终偏大，student 的上限会被 teacher 束缚，验证了文中对“强 teacher 信号抑制潜力”的判断。第四，reference-policy KL 仍然重要；没有它时，蒸馏和 reward 双重驱动会放大策略漂移，稳定性变差。

你给出的全文片段没有包含完整结果表和具体模型规模、数据规模、任务数字，因此无法可靠填写精确参数量、样本量和绝对提升幅度。若要补齐数字，优先查主实验表、ablation 表以及 appendix 中的 training config。
summary.reading_guide: 这篇适合泛读，但不要只看摘要。建议先看 Introduction 里关于 self-distillation 的 policy-gradient 解释，那是全文最有信息量的部分，决定了这篇工作的价值不只是“又一个 RL trick”。然后看方法章节里 reverse KL 梯度恒等式的推导，重点确认三件事：为什么是 reverse KL 而不是 forward KL；为什么 teacher 分支要 stop-gradient；centered log-ratio advantage 是怎么来的。接着看 objective 设计，弄清 verifier reward、distillation、reference KL 三项各自扮演什么角色。实验部分优先看稳定性曲线和消融，不必过度纠结主表排名。真正值得深挖的是两个问题：一是 privileged context 的质量如何影响 token-level advantage 的偏差；二是 positive-advantage gating 会不会让模型错过“从失败轨迹中学局部正确模式”的机会。预计 30–45 分钟可以完成一次有效泛读；若要复现或迁移到 reasoning RL pipeline，再读 appendix 的正则形式和实现细节。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a specific tension in RL with verifiable rewards: the verifier provides sparse sequence-level supervision, while reasoning models benefit from dense token-level learning signals. Prior on-policy self-distillation methods use the same model with privileged context as a teacher, but they are often treated as heuristic auxiliary losses, without a clean policy-gradient interpretation. They also risk reinforcing locally plausible tokens on globally wrong trajectories when the teacher signal is imperfect. SDPG asks how to integrate full-vocabulary self-distillation into KL-regularized RLVR in a principled way, so that sparse verifier rewards and dense privileged supervision can work together without destabilizing training.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining paper in the narrow sense, but it is relevant to the pretrain–post-train interface because it turns self-distillation from a practical trick into an analyzable RL objective. Its value is threefold. First, it gives full-vocabulary reverse-KL self-distillation an exact local policy-gradient interpretation, which clarifies why it can compensate for sparse rewards. Second, it makes the failure mode explicit: privileged context is not automatically beneficial, and without verifier constraints it can amplify token-level preferences on globally incorrect rollouts. Third, the proposed gating and coefficient schedule are really mechanisms for controlling training-signal quality, which is useful beyond RLVR and may transfer to synthetic supervision, process supervision, or mid-training settings. The contribution is best understood as making a class of methods more interpretable and more stable, rather than introducing a new paradigm.
summary_en.technical_approach:
SDPG is built on a KL-regularized policy optimization framework with three supervision sources. The first is the standard RLVR outcome reward. It uses group-based rollouts and group-relative advantages, with normalized standard deviation to stabilize reward normalization under low-variance groups. The second is privileged on-policy self-distillation. The same model is split into two branches: the deployable student conditions on the normal context, while the teacher sees extra privileged information such as demonstrations, direct answers, or reasoning traces. The key choice is to use the exact full-vocabulary reverse KL, D_KL(p_t || SG[q_t]), where the teacher branch is stop-grad. The paper shows that, for a fixed rollout prefix, the student-side gradient of this reverse KL is locally identical to a detached-sampling policy-gradient update whose token-level advantage is a centered log teacher/student ratio. This matters because the distillation term is no longer just imitation; it becomes an advantage-shaping signal over the full vocabulary. The third component is reference-policy KL regularization. Following the RPG view, the main text uses unnormalized forward and reverse KL terms to a fixed reference policy to control policy drift under the combined pressure of verifier rewards and privileged distillation.

Two stabilizers are central. Positive-advantage gating activates or strengthens the distillation signal only when the verifier-side advantage is positive, reducing the chance that the teacher reinforces bad trajectories. A warmup-decay schedule for the distillation coefficient gives dense guidance early, then gradually hands control back to the verifier objective later, limiting teacher-induced ceiling effects. Compared with methods such as RLSD, which fold teacher information into a clipped ratio objective, SDPG treats distillation as an exact, full-vocabulary, interpretable auxiliary policy-gradient signal.
summary_en.experiments:
The experimental section compares SDPG against three families of baselines: pure RLVR/GRPO-style methods, prior self-distillation methods, and SDPG variants with different regularization and stabilization choices. The main conclusion is consistent: SDPG improves both final performance and training stability over RLVR and self-distillation baselines, with the largest gains appearing in the early phase where rewards are sparse and negative advantages are common. The benefit is not only a better endpoint but also smoother learning curves and fewer collapses or oscillations.

The ablations are more informative than the headline result. Exact full-vocabulary reverse KL outperforms sampled-token approximations, suggesting that the teacher distribution carries useful dark knowledge for reasoning token selection. Removing positive-advantage gating makes training more vulnerable to noisy teacher guidance, especially on globally incorrect trajectories. Removing the warmup-decay schedule, or keeping the distillation coefficient too large throughout training, suppresses the student’s eventual potential, matching the paper’s claim that overly strong teacher signals can hurt exploration and final capability. Reference-policy KL also remains important; without it, the combination of reward and distillation leads to larger policy drift and worse stability.

The provided full-text excerpt does not include the final result tables or reliable numeric details such as model size, data scale, or exact improvement margins, so those should not be fabricated. To recover the numbers, the main result tables, ablation tables, and appendix training configurations are the places to check.
summary_en.reading_guide: This is a skim paper, but it is worth reading beyond the abstract. Start with the introduction’s policy-gradient interpretation of self-distillation; that is the conceptual center of the work. Then read the method section around the reverse-KL gradient identity and verify three points: why reverse KL is used instead of forward KL, why the teacher branch is stop-grad, and how the centered log-ratio advantage emerges. After that, read the objective carefully to separate the roles of verifier reward, distillation, and reference KL. In the experiments, prioritize stability plots and ablations over the main benchmark table. The two questions worth thinking about are how privileged-context quality affects token-level advantage bias, and whether positive-advantage gating sacrifices useful local learning signals from failed trajectories. A solid skim should take about 30 to 45 minutes; appendix details matter only if you want to reproduce or adapt the method.

recommendation.zh: 这篇值得从 loss 设计角度细看：把 privileged-context self-distill 写成精确 reverse-KL 很干净，建议直接复现其 ablation，看是否真能稳住 RLVR。
recommendation.en: Worth reading for the loss design alone: casting privileged-context self-distillation as exact reverse-KL is unusually clean; I’d reproduce the ablations to see if it genuinely stabilizes RLVR.

paper.title: Regret Pre-training: Bridging Prior and Posterior Views for Enhanced Knowledge Grounding

summary.core_problem: 在知识 grounding 上，如何同时利用“先验（模型原有参数化知识）”与“后验（给定证据/上下文后的更新）”来减少幻觉与错误引用。
summary.importance: 如果方法成立，属于把“模型知道什么”与“证据告诉它什么”显式对齐的训练信号设计，可能对 RAG/检索增强、引用一致性、以及持续预训练的目标函数有启发。
summary.technical_approach: 提出“Regret Pre-training”概念：用某种 regret/差分信号度量先验输出与后验（有证据条件下）输出的偏离，并把这种偏离转成训练目标，鼓励模型在有证据时向后验收敛、在无证据时保持校准；具体实现细节未知（可能是对比学习/偏好式目标/自蒸馏）。
summary.experiments: 摘要缺失，无法确认是否是从头预训练还是 mid-train、数据来源（检索证据构造方式）、以及相对 baselines（RAG、self-consistency、citation training）的增益幅度。

summary_en.core_problem: How to improve knowledge grounding by explicitly bridging a model’s prior (parametric knowledge) and posterior (evidence-conditioned update) to reduce hallucinations and mis-citations.
summary_en.importance: If validated, it is a training-signal design that aligns “what the model thinks” with “what evidence supports”, potentially informing RAG/citation consistency and continual pretraining objectives.
summary_en.technical_approach: Proposes “Regret Pre-training”: define a regret/difference signal between prior outputs and posterior (with evidence) outputs, and optimize a training objective that pulls the model toward the posterior when evidence exists while keeping calibration otherwise; exact instantiation is unclear (could be contrastive, preference-style, or self-distillation).
summary_en.experiments: No abstract provided; unclear whether this is from-scratch pretraining or mid-training, how evidence is constructed, and gains over baselines like RAG/self-consistency/citation training.

recommendation.zh: 概念听起来像“用证据条件下的自蒸馏做差分训练”，先看它 regret 的定义与负样本构造；没干净对照就当弱信号。
recommendation.en: Sounds like evidence-conditioned self-distillation with a differential objective—check the regret definition and negative construction; without clean controls, treat as weak signal.

paper.title: Internalize the Temperature: On-Policy Self-Distillation as Policy Reheater for Reinforcement Learning
paper.abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards improves the reasoning ability of large language models, but often suffers from entropy collapse, in which increasingly concentrated policies reduce rollout diversity and useful learning signals. Existing remedies either constrain the RL objective (e.g., entropy regularization) or adjust sampling temperature during rollout collection, but these interventions remain external to the model parameters. We propose Temperature-Scaled On-Policy Self-Distil

summary.core_problem: RLVR 在数学和逻辑推理上能提升模型能力，但训练后期容易出现策略熵塌缩：模型分布过于尖锐，rollout 多样性下降，关键分支 token 上的有效梯度变少。TS-OPSD 解决的是“塌缩后如何恢复可探索性，并让恢复后的分布真正写入模型参数”，而不是只在采样时临时调高温度。
summary.importance: 这项工作对预训练研究的直接价值不在于新的预训练目标，而在于它把 RL 后期训练动态中的熵塌缩问题处理成一种轻量的参数修复步骤。它提示了一个实用方向：当模型经过 RL 或持续训练后分布过尖时，可以用自蒸馏做支持集内的概率再分配，保留已有能力，同时给后续优化恢复梯度信号。这对 cooldown、annealing、RLVR 训练续跑、post-train 到 continual pretrain 的接口都有参考意义。
summary.technical_approach: 方法叫 Temperature-Scaled On-Policy Self-Distillation。给定当前模型 logits，先用高温 softmax 构造一个 self-teacher，并对 teacher logits 做 stop-gradient；然后用 full-logits KL 让 student 匹配这个更平滑的分布。关键点是 teacher 完全来自当前策略本身，不需要外部教师模型、奖励条件、特殊上下文或额外推理。由于高温分布满足 p_T(v) ∝ q(v)^(1/T)，token 排名不变，局部支持集不变，只改变分布尖锐程度。这和普通蒸馏不同：普通教师可能给出新的偏好排序，导致 tail token 梯度异常；TS-OPSD 更像是在原策略认可的候选集合里重新分配概率质量。论文还讨论了 forward KL 与 reverse KL 的选择。因为 teacher-student 是 rank-preserving coupling，两种 KL 在行为上的差异会比标准蒸馏场景更小。
summary.experiments: 实验从已经熵塌缩的 RL checkpoint 出发，在 Qwen3-4B-Base 和 Qwen3-8B-Base 上测试。TS-OPSD 能恢复策略熵，同时基本保持下游推理准确率；从恢复后的 checkpoint 继续做 RL，效果优于直接继续 RL，也优于只在 rollout 采样阶段提高 temperature 的做法。这个对比说明收益不只是“采样更随机”，而是模型默认分布被平滑化后，后续 RL 的优化起点更好。分析实验显示，TS-OPSD 主要做 support-preserving probability redistribution：中间表示、top candidate set 和已有推理能力大体保持稳定。全文给出的摘录没有包含具体 benchmark 名称和提升数值，精确数字需要看实验表格与附录。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议 20–30 分钟。先看 Introduction 中对 entropy collapse、rollout reheating 和 policy reheating 的区分，明确它解决的是训练动态问题。然后看 Method 里 p_T(v) ∝ q(v)^(1/T) 这一性质，这是方法成立的核心。实验部分建议重点看三类结果：塌缩 checkpoint 经 TS-OPSD 后熵和准确率如何变化；继续 RL 与 high-temperature rollout 的对照；FKL/RKL 和温度 T 的消融。若关心 RLVR 长程训练，可以深挖它的 token-level entropy 分析和 top candidate set 稳定性分析。

summary_en.core_problem: RLVR improves mathematical and logical reasoning, but later-stage optimization often drives the policy into entropy collapse. The model distribution becomes too sharp, rollout diversity drops, and useful gradients remain only at a small number of high-entropy branch points. TS-OPSD addresses how to restore exploration after collapse and write that effect into the model parameters, instead of only changing the sampling temperature at rollout time.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is mainly about RL training dynamics rather than a new pretraining objective. It gives a lightweight way to repair an over-sharpened policy after RL by redistributing probability mass inside the model’s existing support. This is relevant to RLVR continuation, cooldown or annealing stages, and the interface between post-training and further continual training. The useful lesson is that a smoother default policy can be a better optimization starting point than a sharp policy sampled with an external high temperature.
summary_en.technical_approach: Temperature-Scaled On-Policy Self-Distillation constructs a self-teacher from the current model logits using a high-temperature softmax, with stop-gradient teacher logits. The student is trained with a full-logits KL objective to match this smoother distribution on on-policy rollouts. No external teacher, reward-conditioned model, special context, or extra inference path is needed. The main structural property is p_T(v) ∝ q(v)^(1/T): temperature scaling preserves token ranking and local support while only changing distribution sharpness. This makes the method different from standard knowledge distillation, where teacher-student mismatch can introduce new preference orderings and unstable tail-token gradients. The paper also studies forward KL versus reverse KL; because the teacher and student are rank-preserving coupled, the gap between the two KL choices is narrower than in ordinary distillation.
summary_en.experiments: The experiments start from entropy-collapsed RL checkpoints and evaluate Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base. TS-OPSD restores policy entropy while largely preserving downstream reasoning accuracy. Continuing RL from the restored checkpoint outperforms both direct continued RL and a baseline that only increases sampling temperature during rollout collection. This suggests the improvement comes from a smoother parameterized policy, not merely from noisier sampling. Additional analyses show support-preserving probability redistribution: intermediate representations, top candidate sets, and reasoning behavior remain mostly intact. The provided full-content excerpt does not include exact benchmark names or numerical gains; those need to be checked in the experiment tables and appendix.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim time: 20–30 minutes. Start with the introduction’s distinction between rollout reheating and policy reheating. Then read the method section around p_T(v) ∝ q(v)^(1/T), which is the key design choice. In the experiments, focus on three comparisons: entropy and accuracy before and after TS-OPSD, continued RL from the reheated checkpoint versus standard continued RL, and TS-OPSD versus high-temperature rollout sampling. The KL-direction and temperature ablations are the most useful parts for readers interested in long-running RLVR training.

recommendation.zh: 建议看方法和熵曲线；若能稳定救回 collapse checkpoint，应纳入 RLVR 训练中后期 ablation。
recommendation.en: Read the method and entropy curves; if it reliably rescues collapsed checkpoints, it belongs in mid-to-late RLVR ablations.

paper.title: CAST: Non-Privileged Clipped Asymmetric Self-Teaching with Advantage Flipping for GRPO
paper.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), especially Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), has been widely used to improve reasoning in large language models. However, outcome-level rewards provide only sparse supervision, and group-relative advantages vanish when all sampled trajectories for a prompt are either correct or incorrect. On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) offers dense token-level guidance, but its token preferences are not necessarily aligned with trajectory correc

summary.core_problem: GRPO 等基于验证器的 RLVR 方法提供的是稀疏的结果级奖励信号，存在两个关键局限：(1) 无法告诉模型哪些 token 有助于推理、哪些有损害；(2) 当一个 prompt 采样的所有轨迹全部正确或全部错误时（零方差组），组相对优势消失，这些样本被浪费。On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) 虽然能提供稠密 token 级信号，但它不区分轨迹的正确性就对 token 做对称处理，且常依赖带答案特权的 teacher 上下文。
summary.importance: 针对 RLVR 的稠密监督信号不足和零方差组浪费问题，提出了一种无需特权信息的自教学框架 CAST，在 GRPO 框架内实现了基于轨迹正确性上下文解释 teacher-student gap 的不对称处理。这对 RL 后训练的信号设计有参考价值——提示如何在不引入额外信息的前提下把自蒸馏信号与验证器信号更精细地结合。
